subject: Slowpath regression: coordination, product asks, and customer outreach
messages:
From: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@cartmate.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@cartmate.com
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden slow responses from inference API

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a substantial increase in end-to-end time for a subset of requests hitting your gen endpoint starting ~07:50 PDT. It's not all traffic — roughly 6% of requests to our stream endpoint are taking 3-8x longer than baseline. Our SRE has attached traces and a short timeline. Can your team confirm whether you've deployed anything that might impact warm start or cache behavior?

This is impacting our checkout recommendation flow; we have a high-risk campaign running today and need an ETA for mitigation.

Attachments: cartmate-traces-19mar.zip (linked), timeline.md

Thanks,
Amelia
CartMate SRE

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: sudden slow responses from inference API — quick sync + next steps

Team — forwarding CartMate's alert. Key asks: (1) triage root cause and short-term mitigation, (2) propose a customer-safe timeline and a one-paragraph customer message, (3) decide whether we should enable protective fallback to the smaller model for CartMate only (dedicated route).

Initial notes from our side: the traces show long latency when KV lookup misses spike; could be cache churn on the slowpath. I need a triage owner and a recommended immediate mitigation within 30 minutes to share with the customer.

Marissa — I think you should be on the external thread once we have the mitigation. Karthik/Soojin — can you pair on root cause? Grace/Ben — please prepare a short customer-facing timeline and escalation brief.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: sudden slow responses from inference API — quick sync + next steps

Naomi / team — quick summary from initial triage (Karthik + Soojin):
- We confirmed a rollout yesterday of a kernel selection change for the gen-runtime that reduces tail latencies on long sequences but changed the cache eviction window. On typical workloads this is an improvement; for CartMate's micro-burst profile it appears to cause frequent KV cache eviction leading to repeated slowpath loads.
- Evidence: correlated spikes in backend root cause traces, increased access to model weights on GPU, KV cache-miss rate up from ~4% to ~22% for affected routes (see attached kv-cache-stats.csv).

Short-term mitigations we can execute in the next 30-90 minutes:
A) Temporary protective routing: pin CartMate routes to pre-rollout model variant (safe, low-risk, no config changes to customer) — ETA 15-25 minutes.
B) Increase KV cache capacity for the affected shard group by +25% (faster but requires infra push and careful monitoring) — ETA 45-90 minutes and slight memory pressure risk.
C) Emergency rollback of kernel change (full rollback across fleet) — broader impact and requires approvals, ETA 2+ hours.

Recommendation: A -> implement immediately to stop customer impact while we run a targeted increase (B) in parallel and quantify risk. If A can't be completed quickly, we go to B for the customer only.

I'll prepare the commands and a runbook entry to implement A. Soojin — can you validate that routing pinning will not affect downstream capacity controls?

Karthik
Sr. Staff SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@cartmate.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@cartmate.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Mar 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden slow responses from inference API

Amelia — thanks for flagging and apologies for the disruption. Naomi and the SRE team are on this; we believe we can apply a temporary protective routing that should restore normal response times for your checkout flow within ~20 minutes while we investigate.

Planned immediate steps:
- Route CartMate's production key to the pre-rollout model variant (15-25 minutes).
- Monitor latency and error rates for 30 minutes.
- Share a short post-fix timeline and follow-up RCA within 48 hours.

If you prefer a more conservative approach (we can increase cache capacity for your shard only), we can do that as well; it will take longer and requires a maintenance window for careful monitoring.

I'll keep you posted as soon as we flip the route.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@cartmate.com>, CartMate Ops <ops@cartmate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Mar 2029 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: CartMate update: immediate mitigation completed and next steps

Amelia / CartMate Ops — thank you for your patience. Quick summary of what we completed and next steps: 

What we did (completed Tue 09:20 PDT):
- Implemented temporary protective routing for CartMate production key to the stable model variant (result: 95th percentile latency returned to baseline within 10 minutes).
- Enabled focused telemetry capture and retained traces for your team; attached incident timeline and traces (customer-incident-timeline.pdf, p95-traces.zip).

What we are doing next (work in progress):
- Targeted KV cache capacity bump for affected shard group (ETA 12-24 hours) while we run a controlled test in staging.
- Root cause analysis: we're correlating the kernel selection change with higher cache churn for micro-burst patterns; final RCA within 48 hours.
- Product ask: prioritize a small rollback-safe patch that reintroduces a longer warm window for cached KV entries for routes that match micro-burst signatures. We propose a short RFC and a canary test to validate.

Customer-facing timeline we will publish shortly: a 1-paragraph summary for customer dashboards and a 48-hour follow-up with an RCA and remediation plan.

If you need a bridge/war room for the next steps, we can stand up a 1-hour sync (SRE + product + CartMate) — suggest Thu 10:00 PDT.

Apologies again for the interruption. We're treating this as high priority for both reliability and product follow-through.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: customer-incident-timeline.pdf, p95-traces.zip, kv-cache-stats.csv)
